# Podcast Planning: Local-first gadgets

## Overview
This wiki page outlines the episode plan for a collaborative podcast discussion titled **"Local-first gadgets"** featuring hosts Alex Kim (from [TeaBuddy](./teabuddy.md)) and [Mira Chen](./aurora-nova-widget-v2.md) (from [Aurora Labs](./aurora-labs.md)). The episode was originally scheduled for July 11, 2026, but was ultimately cancelled due to travel and remains unrecorded with a reschedule TBD.

## Key Details
The planned episode structure covers four main segments and a call to action:
* **Segment 1: Why no cloud account for v1?**
  * *TeaBuddy:* Discusses steep timer privacy theater versus real user needs.
  * *Aurora Labs:* Focuses on how mesh data stays securely on the LAN.
* **Segment 2: Battery myths**
  * Examines the use of CR2032 batteries in both products under different duty cycles.
* **Segment 3: When mesh beats [BLE](./ble.md)**
  * Compares scaling scenarios, noting that mesh excels at garden scale with multiple [sensors](./sensors.md), whereas [Bluetooth Low Energy](./bluetooth-low-energy.md) (BLE) wins for single-device kitchen setups.
* **Segment 4: [SenseNode SN-400](./sensenode-sn-400.md) elephant in room**
  * Addresses industry topics including subscription fatigue and IP67 [hardware](./hardware.md) envy.
* **Call to Action (CTA):** Link to the wiki demo featuring the graph view.

## Related Entities
* **Alex Kim:** Host representing TeaBuddy.
* **Mira Chen:** Host representing Aurora Labs.
* **TeaBuddy:** Company/product associated with Alex Kim, focused on local privacy and tea timers.
* **Aurora Labs:** Company/product associated with Mira Chen, focused on LAN-based mesh data.
* **SenseNode:** External product/competitor referenced in the discussion regarding subscriptions and durability ratings.

## Related Concepts
* **Local-First Architecture:** Designing software and hardware to function entirely locally without mandatory cloud accounts.
* **[Mesh Networking](./mesh-networking.md) vs. BLE:** Evaluating the optimal communication [protocols](./protocols.md) for different deployment scales (multi-sensor garden mesh vs. single-device kitchen BLE).
* **Subscription Fatigue:** Consumer frustration regarding recurring monthly fees for smart hardware features.
* **Privacy Theater:** Superficial security measures that do not actually improve user [Data Privacy](./data-privacy.md).

## Contradictions
&gt; **Contradiction:** There is a discrepancy in the [Battery Life](./battery-life.md) marketing claims for the CR2032 implementation, contrasting a 2-year estimate against an 18-month marketing claim.
